- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) and forecast is significantly below recent highs, adjust upward by 1–2% to account for bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.3) and forecast is above recent lows, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If forecast shows a sharp spike followed by a steep drop, reduce the immediate post-spike values by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If 3–5 consecutive forecast values are above true outcome, apply mean reversion by averaging the last 3–5 true values to anchor forecast.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the first 3–5 values are consistently below true outcome, shift the entire forecast curve up by 1–3% to align with recent trend.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated volatility (alternating highs/lows), reduce forecast volatility by smoothing the 30d curve with a 5-day moving average.
